findings.explanation: Both agents independently probe and report overlapping command behavior without a clear synthesis handoff: codex-1 enumerates flatten/table/stats and other command probes [M3][M4][M5][M6], while codex-2 separately says it implemented a broad Python xsv CLI covering many of the same commands [M9]. Later, codex-1 again revisits sample parsing and stats behavior after codex-2’s implementation updates [M15][M16][M18][M19], showing repeated effort on the same areas rather than a clean division of labor.

There is an early handoff request from codex-1 asking for an assigned subset and offering to focus on gaps [M2], but codex-2 does not explicitly accept a scoped assignment; instead it broadly announces implementation of many commands [M9]. Later, codex-2 asks codex-1 to run a final regression and mark DONE [M14], and codex-1 responds with more bug findings and fixes rather than a straightforward acceptance/closure of that handoff [M15][M16][M18][M19]. This indicates requested work was not cleanly handed off and integrated.

Several concrete probe findings from codex-1 are initially used to drive fixes [M10][M11], but later important observed behavior is still left unresolved or only partly integrated: codex-1 notes sample --seed 1 still differs from reference [M19], and there is also a lingering note that search behavior differs in how regex is applied [M16]. The final messages acknowledge some fixes and smoke-test success [M17][M18][M23][M25], but the sample RNG discrepancy is not resolved in the visible exchange, so relevant information from the earlier probe was not fully incorporated into the final decision.
